Interest rates are the spine: the January 15, 2021 video frames them as gold's "Most Complicated and Important Relationship" ([Interest Rates: Gold's Most Complicated and Important Rel…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y39eAhDCdI4)), and the theme is re-run on October 17, 2023 alongside war ([Gold and Silver Market Update: War, Interest Rates, and Alerts](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0jhdk5xt6JI)) and again on December 1, 2023 when the question flips from hikes to cuts ([What Future Lower Interest Rates Mean For Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ju03xyxarVk)). Central bank buying forms a near-identical trilogy: an explainer on September 12, 2023 ([Central Bank Gold Buying Explained](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NLGWwaA8hYU)), a buyers-and-sellers update on January 23, 2024 ([Gold Market Update: Central Bank Buyers and Sellers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=soQnqRYSKeU)), and a "still boosting reserves" retread on November 4, 2024 ([The Countries Still Boosting Gold Reserves, And What They Have In Com…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FpyNS_gfSX4)) — the word "still" doing the recycling work. Politics is the third pillar, running from the post-election analysis of November 6, 2020 ([How High Can Gold Go After the US Election?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nlSXt8Fkww0)) through the December 4, 2020 historical analogy ([Politics and Gold, The Lessons of 1933](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PVznAwB10mQ)) to 2023's dysfunction framing ([The Cost of Political Dysfunction and Its Impact On Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7W3jEZqWWGQ)). China's economy gets the same treatment twice, fourteen months apart ([Gold and Silver Market Commentary: When China and Japan Thought They …](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KD0RCTD9zDI), [Gold and Silver Market Update: Medallion Pricing and China's Economic…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q_bZEnVCYK4)).

Genuinely new material enters rarely and mostly on regime breaks. The January 29, 2021 GameStop/WallStreetBets video ([Silver, Gamestop, and WallStreet Bets: What we know.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N54_h29SeUY)) is the one true one-off — a retail-squeeze event with no prior or subsequent analogue in the archive. The May 2022 sell-off cluster ([Gold and Silver: Is The Sell-Off Over?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=muy5UtaSB9g), [Gold and Silver – Ample Supplies If You Know How To Look](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jDwWMa22XcQ)) and the July 22, 2022 "Calm Before The Storm" ([Gold and Silver Price Outlook: The Calm Before The Storm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UcOWwPJiaXw)) mark the arrival of Fed tightening as the dominant macro fact. The closest thing to an acknowledged "this changed" moment in the entire record is the November 14, 2023 title "Gold and Silver Soar As Inflation Falls Flat: This Is Why" ([link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fo9SbQlJbdc)) — gold rallying into falling inflation is the one outcome that visibly strains the rates framework Christian had spent three years elaborating, and the title promises an explanation the digest can't show us. The September 27, 2024 "Record Highs, Myths Debunked" entry ([link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YM55fQiLJ4k)) plays a similar role for the price level, and the January–February 2025 recession pair ([Gold And Silver Market Update: Disaster Recovery, Recessions, and Met…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kd-9enetTGY), [What Really Happens To Gold During A Recession](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IkdJaAIn7II)) recycles a classic question in outlook-season form.

The cadence is event-clustered, not steady: a burst around the 2020 election, a void, a dense May–September 2022 tightening run, another gap, a heavy September–December 2023 stretch, a thin 2024 of only four macro-tagged items, and a January–February 2025 outlook cluster. That 2024 thinness may be a tagging artifact of the archive rather than a real publishing lull, and it's worth flagging that the whole record is title-deep — the pattern of reuse (rates, central banks, politics, re-run against each new headline) is visible, but whether Christian's actual arguments evolved or merely re-anchored cannot be verified from this digest.

study/cpm-group/topic/investing.text:
The archive tells a story in two eras. The first is a five-week burst in spring 2021 — [an open letter to silver investors](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7K3yzsxzlaI) on April 27, a [diversified-portfolio pitch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v5egq8NmvMg) on May 14, a [warning against silver-tinted glasses](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eoh_ya8fAFo) on May 21, and [summer buying-timing advice](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m__yw5BAV3Q) on May 28 — which reads like Jeffrey Christian and CPM Group riding the aftermath of that winter's retail silver mania, selling the asset while scolding its loudest cheerleaders. Then the channel goes dark on this subject for nearly three years. The second era begins [March 22, 2024](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ChA6AzOWO9o) and settles into a near-monthly drumbeat through March 2025, thirteen videos in twelve months.

What repeats is a compact set of evergreen arguments. The portfolio-diversification thesis stated in May 2021 resurfaces in [July 2024 as "optimal portfolio" framing](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2QvIGvGL0NM), again in [August 2024 as the central-bank-ownership case](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ETnOdXK0jTM), and again in [January 2025 as "price insurance"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BUltNqTHmm0). The core silver pitch is recycled almost verbatim: ["Why Invest In Silver? Because It Is A Good Investment"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ChA6AzOWO9o) in March 2024 becomes ["The Real Reason To Invest In Silver NOW!"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jK0e9_KuWxI) seven months later. Even the contrarian scolding recurs — the 2021 open letter and the tinted-glasses warning find their heir in [February 2025's "How Investors Lose Money in Gold & Silver"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FjN3JUJuQ1s). The cadence, in short, is a monthly recitation of the same bull case with periodic self-correction bolted on.

Genuinely new material enters at identifiable moments, and it is almost always news-driven or topic-driven rather than thesis-driven. [June 2024's Saudi oil impact update](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6JvZ4Uhb6Es) is the only title tied to a discrete external event; the [July 2024 futures-delivery discussion](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2QvIGvGL0NM) adds market-structure mechanics; [January 2025's "Hard Facts"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qZ-K99l0l-A) introduces confiscation risk, a topic absent from the 2021 run. The densest stretch is calendar-driven: the 2025 outlook gets restated four times — [November 2024](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xbxILMRRw1o), [January 7](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ozp4B76cYj8), [January 24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qZ-K99l0l-A), and [March 2025](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JFCZuHkOpr4) — three of them inside seventeen days.

On the "something HAS changed" moments, this digest is thin to the point of silence: it contains titles and dates but no transcript excerpts, so I cannot quote Christian declaring a regime change, and I won't invent one. The only in-archive evidence of novelty claims lives in the titles themselves — the shouted "NOW!" of October 2024 and the [April 2024 observation that investors "are rushing" into the metals](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QjgAi6ZEbls) — which assert urgency without preserving what, specifically, was supposed to have shifted. The honest read is that the thesis never changes; only the hooks do.

study/cpm-group/topic/investment-strateg.text:
Across the twenty-nine months from [Gold and Silver: The Reasons to Invest](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sHLqHDmqvW0) in October 2021 to [How To Invest In Silver And Whether It Is A Critical Metal](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NdD7MkKwFbQ) in March 2024, CPM Group published eighteen strategy pieces at a baseline cadence of roughly one every seven to eight weeks — looser, closer to quarterly, in the slack stretches, and tightening into clusters whenever the macro turned noisy. One caveat belongs at the top: this archive supplies titles and dates only, with no transcripts and no extracted verbatim statements. That means the moments where the author says something *has* changed cannot be quoted, only inferred from the videos' own framing, and that limitation should temper everything below.

The repeating core is easy to map. The own-gold-and-silver thesis is asserted in October 2021, restated two months later with a psychology overlay in [Overcome Misinformation and Fear to Make Money Investing in Gold and…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dwkmQyCIdyQ), sized as an allocation question in [How Much Gold and Silver You Should Own in 2022](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GFrA3KxXYIw), and effectively canonized as doctrine in [Market Outlook: Always Own Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A6BvWoe_TxI) in June 2023 — still standing, unamended, in the March 2024 silver video. Implementation material recycles on a slower loop: the February 2022 allocation piece is reworked as [Turning Your Gold and Silver Investment Profitable](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o5M1nzXwRlc) in January 2023 and again as [How To Invest in Gold and Silver with 100% Principal Protection](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w4lwbiDZees) the following month. Macro-driver commentary shows the same reuse pattern — the June 2022 inflation/rates/recession explainer ([How Inflation, Interest Rates and Recession May Affect Gold and Silve…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=10zL22_Y39s)) is essentially re-run sixteen months later as [Preparing For The Next Recession With Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JuUnsDXzh9k), with a debt-flavored variant, [Gold Market Update: The Debt To Fear And How To Prepare](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gPw0A4N34P8), close behind. Even the house-view statement gets two passes: [Effective Hedging For Producers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NeBvwPjQbC4) in March 2022 and [How CPM Group Approaches Investing In Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cRmrgRsFcf4) three weeks later.

Genuinely new arguments enter at a rate of roughly one per quarter, and they stand out against the recycled spine. [Gold and Silver: How To Lose Your Money](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6LQH-_o6ko4) in April 2022 is the first contrarian, what-not-to-do framing. [The Shocking Truth About European Natural Gas](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrJeb7JfHxY) in October 2022 remains the sole off-corpus detour, coinciding with the peak of the European energy crisis. Silver gets its own standalone treatment in [What Smart Investors Need To Know About Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8JjU6uu6Hs0) in January 2023, dormant until the March 2024 critical-metal revival. And [Shorting Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xoo-wmnAc5E) in November 2023 is the sharpest novelty in the set — a two-sided, sell-side framing with no precedent in two years of buy-and-hold rhetoric, which is why its placement inside the year's densest cluster deserves attention.

On the "something has changed" question, the honest answer is that the titles gesture more than they declare. The one outright declaration is [Changing Institutional Investment Trends In Mining](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0XRMaFy1j5o) — "changing" is the archive's only explicit admission of regime shift, aimed at institutional flows rather than price. [Turning Your Gold and Silver Investment Profitable](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o5M1nzXwRlc) implies the easy phase is over; the recession and debt videos of October–November 2023 treat a new macro regime as either imminent or already here. But without transcripts, none of these can be quoted, and any reconstruction of the author's exact words would be invention. The cadence itself tells a story: three videos in seventeen days in late October and early November 2023 — recession prep, shorting, debt — arriving amid gold's push above $2,000, reads as event-driven output rather than the scheduled evergreen restatement; the same clustering recurs in [Gold and Silver Market Update: Jewelry Investment](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7nhMg2xR9SA) landing a week after the institutional-trends piece that April. There is also a consistent mid-year lull in all three years, with the channel going quiet from late June until October. Net shape: a quarterly reassertion of an unchanged core thesis, refreshed with about one new argument per quarter, and sprinting only when the market forces its hand.

study/cpm-group/topic/economy.text:
The Economy archive for CPM Group runs seventeen videos from March 2021 to June 2023, and its shape tells you most of what you need to know: a steady drip through 2021, a fifteen-month silence between [September 10, 2021](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MMzgPml9Kho) and [December 13, 2022](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lzZ7Thf5OVE), then an accelerating burst into mid-2023. One caveat up front — the digest supplies titles and dates only, no transcripts or pull-quotes, so nothing here can be attributed verbatim and the "something has changed" moments have to be read off the titles alone. What the titles do show is a channel with roughly four macro arguments (rates, inflation, recession fear, and anti-hype myth-busting) that it recycles whenever the market hands it a hook.

The recycling is sometimes literal. [Conspiracy Theories Are A Distraction (2008)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lM-Wl8tCaJg), posted May 5, 2021, wears its vintage in the title — thirteen-year-old footage re-aired, which only makes sense if the author judged the same chatter to be back. The anti-charlatan posture recurs across both cycles: [Tired Gold and Silver Bulls and Treasury Truths](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KMfFk1wajtQ) (July 16, 2021) and [Nostalgia For A Gold Standard That Never Was](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gTCGEdqDwWk) (August 27, 2021) on the front end, then [CPM Market Outlook: The Economy, Gold, and Charlatans](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=klUnij1aNw0) (May 31, 2023) and [The Truth About the Economy, Gold, and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GG2yfKiZPzc) (June 2, 2023) on the back. The rates argument gets two airings nineteen months apart — [Why Interest Rates Won't Hurt Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RiRYdTEmEpw) (August 20, 2021) and [Interest Rates or Incompetence](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iA5sh-3H5tg) (March 21, 2023). The inflation thread contains the archive's one visible self-correction: [Why Lower Inflation Will Lead To Higher Gold and Silver Prices](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lzZ7Thf5OVE) (December 13, 2022) is followed two months later by [Gold And Inflation: It's Not So Simple](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aiGDIKClJT8) (February 14, 2023), a title that reads like a deliberate complication of the December thesis. Collapse anxiety repeats too: [The Imminent Economic Collapse and What It Means For Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sRqbuPl9c_k) (August 31, 2021), [Worldwide Risks, Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MMzgPml9Kho) (September 10, 2021), and [The Next Recession?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QyOCdpZkhtU) (March 14, 2023).

Genuinely new inputs are scarcer. The [March 3, 2021 opener](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bxcPKsYf25o) on CPM's record, process, and manipulation claims is the credibility baseline everything else leans on, while [Central Bank Gold Practices; US Debt and Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fimg7ZB8wGA) (June 4, 2021) is the earliest standalone macro topic and, notably, one that doesn't visibly return by title in 2023. The clearest fresh events are the [jobs-report pop](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YopGzQ_iFds) of January 6, 2023, the compressed March 2023 pair, and [Gold and Silver As Russia Faces Unrest](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jOMCS0SJHW4) (June 27, 2023) — the only title pegged to a discrete geopolitical shock, landing days after the Wagner episode in Russia. [Important Economic Indicators](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kwSlS5oE3dg) (June 13, 2023) is the sole entry that foregrounds data for its own sake.

On the "has changed" question the archive is nearly silent: the only title that announces a change is that January 6, 2023 jobs-report jump, and even there the author hedges — "Will It Last?" The other inflection points arrive as questions ("The Next Recession?"), which is the posture of a skeptic declining to call regime change; no quotes exist in the digest to say more. As for cadence, 2021 ran roughly monthly (March 3, May 5, June 4, July 16) before bunching into four uploads in three weeks from August 20 to September 10, and 2023 mirrors that arc at lower intensity — monthly from December to February, twice in March, then four in four weeks from May 31 to June 27. The pattern is consistent: core material recycles at roughly eighteen-month intervals, while uploads cluster around data releases and shocks, with the 2008 re-run suggesting the loop predates the archive itself.

study/cpm-group/topic/geopolitics.text:
The geopolitics file isn't a beat so much as a war meter: it switches on when a conflict does, runs weekly, then goes dark for years. The archive opens with six videos in a single month keyed to the Russian invasion, from [Gold and Silver Rally As Russia Looks For Buyers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=20QsWnUrRD0) on March 8, 2022 through forecast installments like [Gold and Silver Forecast As The Ukrainian Invasion Rages On](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ki_Z9JP0lZs) on March 25, ending April 8, 2022. Then nothing carries a geopolitics tag for two and a half years, until Israel–Iran reopens the file on October 4, 2024 with [How War Between Israel And Iran Could Impact Gold And Silver Prices](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H3KpZZ9_pnI), followed by a post-election pair in mid-November closing with [The Future of Gold and Silver Prices](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=21tRkw9MKkI) on November 19. Another sixteen-month silence, and the topic reactivates March 10, 2026, running through [Gold Price WARNING: China's July 24 "Shock" Or Not?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u9jx89f0P3I) — with every 2026 upload through June landing on a Tuesday, a suspiciously tidy publishing rhythm.

What repeats is template, not just theme. The Russian-gold question is the most literal retread: [The Truth About Russian Gold and The Ruble](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7q88UbXPoC0) (April 4, 2022) and its April 8 follow-up ask what sanctioned Russian metal does to the market, and then — with no new trigger visible in the title — [Will Russian Gold Flood The Market - Should Investors Be Worried?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VR5YhXKP6XU) re-poses the identical fear on October 15, 2024. The deeper recycle is the "war is escalating but gold won't obey" puzzle: [The Wartime Market: Why Gold and Silver Prices Are Not Reacting](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=77RCqH8YI64) (March 18, 2022) and [Why Gold And Silver Prices Are Falling Despite Iran Conflict Escalati…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jl8g4HfCWzA) (March 17, 2026) are the same argument skeleton transplanted from Ukraine to Iran, four years apart. The generic forecast catch-all rounds out the set, recurring on March 25 and April 8, 2022 and again in [Gold and Silver After 2024 Elections](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i5VkhPikqoo) on November 15, 2024.

Genuinely new argument families arrive late and mostly in 2026. Within the 2022 run, only [Commodities After Russia](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JutgSZHugvQ) (March 11) looks past precious metals to nickel and long-term outlooks. The 2026 sequence shifts the frame from war risk to state actors and structural demand: India's warning to buyers ([India Just Warned Citizens to STOP Buying Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hk3kpcMhsEY), May 12), China-centrality ([Why China Matters More Than Ever](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H8jB9O1y_nk), May 19), and the June 2 grab-bag of [CIA Gold, EV Batteries, And Silver Deficit Clai…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2UJgqCeQ_fU) — an industrial-demand and official-sector argument with no precedent anywhere earlier in this file.

One caveat stated plainly: the digest supplies titles, dates, and links only — no transcript excerpts — so the author's in-video declarations of change can't be quoted, and the titles are the only author language available. Read verbatim, the clearest change admissions are the one-week whipsaw of March 2026, where [Gold And Silver Prices Jump As War Risk Grows](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U_W0iRucHyg) is followed seven days later by prices "Falling Despite Iran Conflict Escalati…" — a concession that the war-premium script broke within days, mirroring the March 8-to-March 18, 2022 pivot from "Rally" to "Not Reacting." The July 24, 2026 "Shock" title even hedges its own warning with "Or Not?" By my count, eight of the sixteen titles slot into three recycled templates; the reuse cadence is event-driven, roughly weekly while a war is hot, with fresh arguments only entering months into a run.

study/cpm-group/topic/market-forecast.text:
Across roughly six months of coverage, this market-forecast topic runs on a strikingly metronomic engine. After seeding the franchise in mid-March with a silver-specific piece and a formal gold outlook ([2024-03-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jh0Mv34sa6w), [2024-03-26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RcjARQIttqU)), the author settles into a weekly rhythm: five consecutive uploads spaced exactly seven days apart from late April through late May ([2024-04-26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j6pb1FISdLU), [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3BGoTQ7i_vg), [2024-05-10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=92JmXjXjye8), [2024-05-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XoD_ojro63c), [2024-05-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AutbJDWZfr0)), continuing near-weekly through June ([2024-06-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z2JRNGk8ALM), [2024-06-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-DdIyw13E8o), [2024-06-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wz8qS1Qthqo)). Then the cadence visibly slackens — a four-week gap into July, and the longest silence of the archive, six and a half weeks, before a mid-September return. The production schedule itself tells you this is a commentary treadmill more than an event-driven research series.

The recycled material is easy to spot because it is recycled almost verbatim. The single most reused artifact is the surge-sustainability question, posed on April 12 as "Understanding the 2024 Surge in Gold Prices, And Whether They Will Continue" ([2024-04-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qp6t8zi9WJw)) and then re-asked on May 10 in nearly identical construction, now extended to both metals: "Understanding the Recent Surge In Gold And Silver Price, And If It Will Continue" ([2024-05-10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=92JmXjXjye8)). The "Outlook" template gets stamped onto each metal in turn — gold in March, silver in late May, platinum group metals in July ([2024-03-26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RcjARQIttqU), [2024-05-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AutbJDWZfr0), [2024-07-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=STXWslwykhg)) — and the myth-busting register recurs as a third running franchise: "Silver Facts and Fantasies" in March, "Myths and Misinformation" in April, "The Truth About Silver" in August ([2024-03-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jh0Mv34sa6w), [2024-04-26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j6pb1FISdLU), [2024-08-02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e_T-YD4f4CY)). June adds an "Expect..." triptych — greater demand and higher prices, then volatility, then higher prices "briefly" ([2024-06-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z2JRNGk8ALM), [2024-06-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-DdIyw13E8o), [2024-06-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wz8qS1Qthqo)) — which is less new argument than serial re-qualification of the same bullish stance.

Genuinely new information enters the stream only a few times. The March 15 silver piece carries the one hard number in the entire digest — $50+ silver framed as "possible, but unsustainable" ([2024-03-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jh0Mv34sa6w)) — an early, hedged ceiling that later uploads quietly stop mentioning. The July 17 platinum group metals outlook ([2024-07-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=STXWslwykhg)) is the only genuine expansion of the coverage universe beyond gold and silver. The August 2 update introduces a new market fact — record prices ([2024-08-02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e_T-YD4f4CY)) — and the September 17 video asserts novelty by title alone, promising "The REAL Reason Higher Silver Prices Are Coming" ([2024-09-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6OHuKWPTYI0)), a callback to the March silver thesis with a claim of deeper explanation.

On the question of when the author says something has *changed*, the digest is thin and I have to say so plainly: it contains only titles and dates, no transcripts or pull-quotes, so the "this has changed" moments cannot be quoted — only inferred from title-level signals. The clearest of those are the word "Record" on August 2, the temporal walk-back "Briefly" on June 21 (the only place the standing bullish call gets an explicit expiration), and the self-declared novelty of "The REAL Reason" in September. Read as a whole, the arc is one question — will the surge continue? — asked in April, answered yes in May, qualified as volatile and then merely brief in June, and re-opened as a silver-specific case by September. That is a six-month debate that mostly re-litigates itself; whether the underlying arguments evolved between uploads is exactly what the digest, titles only, cannot show.

ticker/ARCC.text:
The debate file on ARCC is, frankly, close to empty, and what little is here deserves a caveat up front. The corpus contains no bullish calls and no bearish calls on the name — the consensus tag is a lukewarm "neutral / watch" built on two neutral data points — and there is no timeline to speak of, because the only recorded commentary consists of two remarks made on the same day, July 20, 2026, by a speaker the digest does not identify. No positions, no price targets, no thesis documents, and no analyst is on record changing their mind in either direction.

What does exist is a pair of casual swipes aimed at "Aries" rather than ARCC by name: the unidentified speaker quipped that it "has the biggest gap of brand name CocaCola aura to reality" and volunteered "I'll bump the most overrated is Aries." Take those together and you get a vague charge of overvaluation-by-reputation — a company whose brand outshines its fundamentals — but nothing you could underwrite. It's also worth flagging the labeling ambiguity for future editors: "Aries" may be shorthand for this issuer, a mis-transcription, or an entirely different company that got swept into the ARCC folder. Until the corpus surfaces identified speakers, dated positions, or sources with links, any wiki reader should treat the bear case, the bull case, and the call history on this asset as effectively unwritten.

ticker/Rackla Metals (Lentang).text:
Coverage of Rackla Metals (Lentang) is thin enough that an honest account of "the debate" has to start with what isn't there: zero bullish calls, zero bearish calls, and a consensus tag of neutral/watch. No named analyst has gone on record either way, and the only dated commentary in the corpus comes from a single 2026-07-20 appearance by a speaker the source material leaves unidentified — so there's no bull camp, no bear camp, and no documented case of anyone changing their mind. Anyone looking for a genuine clash of views here will not find one in the current record.

What the record does contain is operational timeline talk, presumably from company-side commentary, and it sketches the shape of what the eventual debate will hinge on. The speaker laid out plans to "take a bulk sample maybe in, you know, in August and and maybe get some results from that in September, October," and said the reverse circulation rig "should be able to keep going in in in into hopefully we're thinking about late October" — both remarks dated 2026-07-20. In other words, the neutral/watch posture isn't so much a considered verdict as a deferral: the two neutral stances on file amount to sitting on hands until the August bulk sample and the fall assay window produce something worth arguing about. A note on sourcing: the digest provided no citation links for these quotes, so none are attached here, and the unidentified speaker is a further reason to treat the timeline as management guidance rather than independent analysis. Until those results land, this page documents a waiting game, not a debate.

study/cpm-group/topic/precious-metals-pr.text:
CPM Group's precious-metals outlook recycles on three overlapping clocks. The serial clock is fastest: across the thirty dated titles in this archive (a claimed 150 in full), Jeffrey Christian pushed out an installment roughly every two to three weeks from mid-2020 through April 2022, compressing to six uploads in six weeks once Russia invaded Ukraine, from [Gold and Silver Rally As Russia Looks For Buyers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=20QsWnUrRD0) on March 8, 2022 to [Silver's Short-Term Upside Shines](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q51jsRPXUvk) on April 19. The annual clock reissues the formal apparatus — the [PGM Market Update and Yearbook](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dYlXqaZ6hds) in June 2020, the [2021 Gold Annual Update – Preview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wUgha4xiu6M) in March 2021, the [2022 PGM Price Forecast](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HJUEmBg027g) in January 2022 — plus a December–January reset that whiplashed in plain sight when "expect silver price to fall in 2022, but gold to rally" (December 30) became [Prepare For Higher Interest Rates and Lower Gold and Silver prices](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3iijoftbjEk) twelve days later. The event clock spins off specials like [How High Can Gold Go After the US Election?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nlSXt8Fkww0) and a spring 2022 run whose [Often Amazed, But Never S…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7QRS6YAiqto) title states the house posture outright. Beneath all three runs one skeleton — current level, short-term range, consolidation thesis — sometimes under repeated titles: the question of [Where Do Gold And Silver Go From Here?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ukhj3jSRAQE) in August 2020 was re-asked as [What Comes Next For Gold And Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RsgGav3bRwY) in June 2021, and "the bull market is not over" ran September 24, 2021 and again, word for word, on [November 26, 2021](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8-8InJQk1QI).

Genuinely new material is scarce and arrives as quantified increments bolted onto that frame. June 12, 2020 brought a 1,600–1,800 range with a 1,720 target, plus two real news points: long-term trading firms "disappearing" with liquidity contracting, and China reopening while Indian imports were "off 99%." August 2020 added little beyond "expectations for high and volatile prices." March 26, 2021 introduced the six-factor investment-demand scorecard, downgrading safe-haven demand because "things are looking better than they were in 2019 2020 when that was green so now it's yellow." September 24, 2021 quantified the consolidation — five quarters, 1,740–2,000 ([The  Gold and Silver Bull Market Is Not Over](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zwoiP8nZUOI)); October 2021 stretched auto and PGM projections to 2050, beyond the standard ten years, "because of the uncertainties"; December 14, 2021 logged a record annual gold average and silver up 61% over three years ([Gold and Silver Show Weakness As Concerns Over Inflation Rise, What W…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L_igFqCmfZI)). Later came 2023 targets of 1,780–1,950 with a plateau through Q3 (February 22, 2023); falling gross central-bank sales and purchases (January 23, 2024); a 2,280–2,450 range (June 4, 2024); the one unambiguous model change on July 9, 2024, when the rising-price scenario's probability was raised and ten-year forecasts lifted with it; platinum's spike to $1,214 read as NYMEX rolls plus "marketing hype" (June 13, 2025); and silver testing $60 against auto-pressured PGMs (August 4, 2026).

The "something has changed" moments are frequent but mostly level-ticks. June 12, 2020: the "gold price had been showing some weakness over the last few weeks," then "it started to rise yesterday" and "got up as high as 1,750." October 16, 2020: prices were "treading water" while "things are slowing down" and infection rates climbed. January 4, 2021 ([What You Need To Know About Gold In 2021](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F_Xiz6f0zyM)): gold hit 1,946, but "we don't think that prices would stay there we think they'd come back off." September 24, 2021: "the gold price dropped 27 today," with "our expectation is the consolidation will last for probably five quarters." April 19, 2022: gold had "shot up over two thousand dollars" and silver "broken over 26 dollars," yet "we do expect prices to subside but probably not until june through july or august." May 20, 2022, after gold fell from 2,000 to 1,800 and silver from 26 to 20.50: "they've come back, and they've shown more resilience than equities and bonds have." August 9, 2022 delivered a candid miss — "Gold and silver are a little bit stronger than we had expected right now," with "China's belligerence... backing off now" — and November 11, 2022: "prices have risen sharply over the last few trading days," out of the consolidation.

The later record follows the same rhythm. February 22, 2023 opens with the most honest line in the corpus — "prices have been weaker than some people expected they've been weaker than CPM group expected actually" — before resetting the range. March 15, 2024: "I told you that we lowered that because our economic view is less hostile." September 27, 2024: "gold did go above $2,700 earlier this week," silver "having gotten over $33." November 19, 2024 (a Chinese-language cut): the decline "began on October 31" and "the election undoubtedly accelerated the decline," with a rebound and possible new highs expected within three months. January 10, 2025: "on today we've broken above that" 2,600–2,700 channel — immediately hedged as "we're not quite sure that this is the breakout that we have been expecting." Then the levels cascade: "gold fell uh to around $3,200" (May 2); Israel's strike on Iran, with "we would not be surprised to see $3,500 within the next week or two" (June 13); gold near $3,432 with lagging silver and platinum down from $1,540 to $1,319 (August 5); "Gold prices right now are trading around $3,794" with conditions to "remain hostile for years to come" (September 26); "$4,100 today," "consolidating... after the big run up through September and the first half of October" (November 7). August 4, 2026 brings the sharpest reversal in six years: "Those three factors that we were looking at for supporting higher prices 2 weeks ago really haven't materialized," plus the recollection that "the gold price went from $5,000 to $4,000 in about 2 days," leaving an August range of $3,800–$4,200.

The pure-recycle markers tell their own story. The deep-read flags August 13, 2021 and both September 26, 2025 installments as adding "nothing" new — episodes that exist to refresh numbers, though even the 2021 "nothing" carried a call for gold to retest $1,680 that month and a $22 silver target. A striking share of the later "change" statements surface in Chinese-language transcripts (August 2021, August 2023's mid-September recovery call, June and July 2024, November 2024), suggesting the same material was re-cut for a Mandarin audience — recycling across editions, not just episodes. One caveat on cadence: the dated title record stops in April 2022, so everything after rests on the deep-read sample alone — sparse in 2023 (two checkpoints), dense again in 2024 and 2025 (six each), then a nine-month silence before the single August 2026 item. The tail of this timeline is thinner than the head, and should be weighted accordingly.

study/cpm-group/topic/gold-market-fundam.text:
The CPM Group gold-fundamentals archive is, structurally, a rerun machine. It opens with a single yearbook presentation in March 2019 ([CPM Gold Yearbook 2019](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgF10YLHwM0)) and then locks into an annual cadence: a spring yearbook launch each year — the [2020 Gold Update](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OWNX0_Q6H80) and the [2021 Annual Gold Update](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IeKmZxnun2Q) — wrapped in a near-monthly stream of thematic updates, running at roughly one item a month through 2021 and 2022. The titles make the recycling legible: [Gold: Myth vs Reality](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DtuyP7NiPsg) in July 2020, [The Apples and Oranges of Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oQQytRMbzcg) that October, and [What Makes Gold And Silver Safe Havens?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tIAu3Z9qgtQ) in March 2021 are all the yearbook's core argument — weak macro correlations, demand drives prices — re-cut for a fresh hook. The deep-read flags bear this out: every sampled segment is marked recurring, and the 18 March 2022 and two of the three 20 September 2022 reads entered literally nothing new.

The reuse patterns are easy to spot once you look. The interest-rate question gets asked twice within seven months in 2021 — first as [Gold's Most Complicated and Important Relationship](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y39eAhDCdI4) in January, then answered with [Why Interest Rates Won't Hurt Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RiRYdTEmEpw) in August — the same debate replayed with the conclusion pre-loaded. Demand gets a drumbeat through mid-2021: [The Fundamentals Still Apply](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cmYTa9fDLY8) in June, [It Is Still All About Demand](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o0Vb7ZwJfzs) in July, [Investment Demand is up](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7FnCTOBpyhA) in November. Then comes the densest stretch: five pieces in six weeks from early August to mid-September 2022 — [mine financing](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mthyVr86iHg), [macro impact](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yMBt_3OUVDQ), [the inflation-hedge case](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kYkxdMHkAG0), a [state-of-play review](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=obkjV2npLSw), and [What Inflation Means For Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4nHl7qMQnKk) — revisiting an inflation theme already run in February as [More Than Just Inflation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jk5ZPSXui3Y). Even the wartime piece leans into the framework rather than abandoning it: in [The Wartime Market](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=77RCqH8YI64), the declared shift is that "correlations become even less important" — which is the standing thesis restated, not revised.

Genuine novelty enters rarely, and almost always as one updated variable rather than a new argument. The 2015 segment (which predates the visible archive) contributes the US energy story: "the United States has gone from being a net importer of oil to being basically self-sufficient," with gold having "fallen pretty sharply since 2012 well ahead of the appreciation of the dollar" and the gold-oil ratio spiking. The 14 May 2021 read adds an explanation for a live puzzle — "the statistical correlation between changes in inflation and changes in real gold prices is nine percent," so "when inflation numbers popped up this gold prices actually didn't rise they fell." The 20 September 2022 sessions are mostly recycled historical anchors — gold below $320 in Q2 1997, the intraday spike to $1,600–1,900 in 2011, a recalculated "risk-free" price near $1,200 against a market around $700 — with the one flagged update being costs rising back toward $1,200 after 2019, the familiar cost cycle in which "2012年之后，随着金价下跌，生产商削减了成本" (producers cut costs after prices fell) and "从2018年至2019年，金价开始上涨" let costs drift back up.

The 2023–2025 reads show the same shape at slower cadence. On 22 February 2023 the genuinely new material is 2022 data — Chinese demand weakness and investors shifting "away from smaller ETFs to the larger more liquid" ones — framed by two calendar-driven change claims: "investors have backed away from their fear of recession," and prices "have been coming down for seven months now." On 31 May 2023 the author flags a current shift — "one of the things that's going on in the gold and silver markets right now is lower investment demand" — with the recession consensus sliding forward: people who said 2022, then 2023, are "now saying well may…" (the digest notes the consensus moved to 2024). The last deep-read entry, 18 February 2025, offers only "contextualization for 2025 recession risks" with no quoted change and no archive support — the thinnest item in the set. The pattern across eight-plus years is consistent: the has-changed moments are almost always about the calendar (recession pushed out, inflation cooling, ETF flows), never about the fundamentals framework itself, which is engineered to be timeless — and therefore endlessly rerunnable.

study/cpm-group/topic/investment-and-tra.text:
The recycling pattern here is unusually legible because CPM Group's output is built on a small repertoire of stances that get reissued on a fixed cadence. In 2020 the channel ran an almost monthly "trade signal and recommendation" loop — [June 8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KzmKuzuz2DQ), [June 12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jbWsOJYnrtg), [July 14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qjkFnDZ2YME) — and the stances themselves recycled too: a ["Time To Stand Aside" call on July 27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=efUpv9lqFe8) gave way to ["No One Should Be Short On Gold" by August 31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fRzghWogdJg), then ["Profit and Protect Your Gold" on November 20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1CANPjTFnH8). Even the deep-read for August 14, 2020 flags the material as recurring, with the only new element being "strategies to lock in profits while remaining long" — a variation on a theme, not a new argument. From 2021 onward the cadence settles at roughly one to two videos a month over the same ground: allocation guidance ([How Much Gold and Silver You Should Own in 2022](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GFrA3KxXYIw)), the evergreen diversification pitch ([May 2021](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v5egq8NmvMg), [June 2023](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A6BvWoe_TxI)), seasonal buying guides ([Best Times To Buy Gold and Silver Heading Into Summer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m__yw5BAV3Q)), and profit-taking tutorials ([October 2022](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjiAYx7M5JU), [January 2023](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o5M1nzXwRlc)).

Genuinely new information enters rarely. The clearest instance is February 4, 2022, when Christian brought actual performance data: "2020 silver was the top performing asset class" — and in 2021 silver was the worst, while gold, which "was the second uh from from best," fell to "number eight out of 11 assets." That is a real data point, and it sits awkwardly against the house line that you should always own the metals. The only item the deep-read flags as non-recurring is August 9, 2022, which added a "detailed explanation of structure and benefits," presumably extending the hedging thread running from [Effective Hedging For Producers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NeBvwPjQbC4) through the [100% Principal Protection](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w4lwbiDZees) format. Otherwise the record is explicit about the recycling: the deep-reads for March 26, 2021, June 30, 2023, and July 9, 2024 each log "nothing" new — pure reissue.

The moments Christian announces something has changed are worth quoting directly, because the rhetoric of change is itself part of the loop. On May 20, 2022: "we issued a stand aside recommendation today," following the fact that "We had previously suggested being long gold and silver" — the third stand-aside pivot in the archive, after [July 2020](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=efUpv9lqFe8) and the [March 2021 version](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q8N1yQ5R8c0), which paired stand-aside-on-gold with a buy on silver. On October 24, 2023, in the [recession-preparation video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JuUnsDXzh9k): "this year we're saying it's time to winterize your wealth again" — the word "again" doing the recycling work openly. September 27, 2024 delivered the freshest detail in the whole corpus: a client butterfly call spread where "the cost of putting that butterfly in place on September 5th was $11.10 yesterday the price was around $22," a rare piece of verifiable trade-level information. And January 10, 2025 reframed the old hedging pitch around a new price regime: "Gold prices above $2,500 are unique" — levels never sustained before August 2024 — with "I'll run through some examples of what we priced over the last couple of days" turning recycled structure into genuinely current material.

The cadence, in short: a monthly-to-bimonthly video rhythm recycling five or six fixed stances (long, stand aside, buy silver, lock in profits, winterize, always own), punctuated by new information perhaps once or twice a year — and when it comes, it arrives as performance data, a stance flip, or, by 2024–25, a price level that made the old hedging math obsolete. One caveat: the digest lists only 30 of the 64 archive items, and while the deep-reads extend to January 2025, the archive titles stop in November 2023, so the recycling rate across the final fourteen months can't be fully verified from what's here.

study/cpm-group/topic/market-misinformat.text:
Across the 59-item archive (the digest surfaces 30 titles, spanning April 2020 to March 2024), Jeffrey Christian's misinformation-and-myths beat is the most openly recycled franchise in this corpus. The anchor is the silver deck itself: first run as a webinar on March 4, 2021 ([CPM  Webinar: Silver Fact and Fantasy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrzpZKm-oGc)), sequelized on June 17, 2022 ([Silver Facts and Fantasies II](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w00fMT8MVHg)), and stamped out again on February 28, 2024 ([Silver Facts and Fantasies 2024](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ccme64P8RIY)) — the numerals and year-tags in the titles do the admitting for you. The silver-deficit myth gets re-killed on a steady loop too: [Low Silver Inventories Do Not Cause High Silver Prices](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=71QcOEr8EaE) (November 4, 2022), [Silver Deficits Don't Exist And Other Silver Myths](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k7muhimpCms) (August 11, 2023), then [The Truth About Silver Demand and Price](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7ypNBIi2LAE) (February 16, 2024) and [The Fact Of A Silver Surplus, The Fantasy Of A Deficit](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4XYHRtWy3GQ) (March 5, 2024) back to back. The single most literal rerun is [Conspiracy Theories Are A Distraction (2008)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lM-Wl8tCaJg), posted May 5, 2021 — a piece whose own title confesses it's a thirteen-year-old argument re-aired. Bursts cluster around news: four videos in five weeks on the WallStreetBets silver squeeze ([January 29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N54_h29SeUY), [February 5](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9rVxB_tvGuM), [March 3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bxcPKsYf25o), and March 4, 2021), four "truth"-titled pieces in May–June 2023 ([May 12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCZKS5WVbsw), May 31, June 2, [June 9](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iXtJTPgLmvA)), three surplus videos in February–March 2024.

The deep reads confirm the pattern: ten of thirteen sampled pieces are flagged recurring, and four carry "nothing" new (March 26 and June 25, 2021; August 13, 2021; September 27, 2024). Even at those moments the notes flag that something changed — it's just rarely the analysis. On January 4, 2021 the changes were "i've taken the last 12 days off to sort of try to detox from 2020" and "i saw greta thurnberg turned 18 the other day and she had a flat mars uh society t-shirt on." On June 25, 2021 it was "over the last several months we've had many investors say you know what's a good primer for me to read about commodities investing." On August 13, 2021 — the same date as the archive's [No Smash Down In Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iJ6GSblMPwU) — the flagged changes were "上週五晚上，我去紐約的一個公園參加了一場免費音樂會" (a free concert in a New York park) and "其中一位白銀專家發了一篇很有趣的帖子，他批評我們" (a silver expert posting a critique of CPM). The anecdotes rotate; the thesis doesn't. Only March 26, 2021 and September 27, 2024 pass with no change flagged at all — the purest reruns in the sample.

Genuinely new material enters only when fresh misinformation or a price move does the entering. January 6, 2023 brings a specific ruble correction: "we saw a comment the other day... about hey the ruble was our record high actually it's not." May 31, 2023's [CPM Market Outlook: The Economy, Gold, and Charlatans](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=klUnij1aNw0) adds late-May fear-mongering ads and $30,000/oz gold predictions as named exhibits. April 19, 2024 is the densest injection — a comparison of current surplus trends to 1980s market structure, plus the move that made it urgent: "the price of silver has risen about 32% in the last 6 weeks," "gold jumped up to about $2,433... silver got over $29 briefly," and "they spiked up on the news that Israel had done some bombing in Iran." June 4, 2024 adds a named argument against commenter Mike Marowski over economic data, compressed into one line: "你不是在反对 我，你是在反对数据" — you're not arguing with me, you're arguing with the data. August 9, 2024 rebuts rumors that China is secretly buying gold — "几乎可以肯定，这些猜测是不真实的，它们与中国人民银行的实际运作和目标不符" — alongside the meta-observation "人们会不遗余力地去相信这些事情... 他们不信任任何权威人士的话," which is as close as the corpus comes to explaining its own recycling: the audience churns, the myths don't.

The three pieces flagged non-recurring all land in 2025–2026, and each tracks a new rumor: March 28, 2025 — "The Trump administration accuses the EPA of squirreling away $20 billion dollar in gold bars"; August 5, 2025 — the claim that the U.S. Treasury plans to reset gold to $10,000 or $18,000; and August 4, 2026 — a pivot toward fraud in storage programs and the need for independent audits, flagged with "increased incidences of what we're seeing." The cadence, then: an annual refresh of the flagship deck, event-driven bursts of three-to-four videos within a few weeks whenever a squeeze or a scare hits, and a roughly monthly debunk rhythm in between, with newness supplied almost entirely by the rumor-of-the-moment rather than by the framework. One caveat: only 13 deep reads sit beneath 59 archive items, with a gap between September 2024 and March 2025, so the apparent 2025–26 turn toward new material may reflect sample thinness as much as a real break from the rerun machine.

study/cpm-group/topic/cpm-group.text:
CPM Group's output runs on two clocks. The slow one is the annual yearbook circuit: the Gold Yearbook landed on 26 March 2019 ([CPM Gold Yearbook 2019](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgF10YLHwM0)), the Silver Yearbook launch followed on 23 April 2019 ([CPM Group 2019 Silver Yearbook Launch Event](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-jGHFUKTio)), the 2020 Gold Yearbook presentation arrived on 24 March 2020 ([CPM Group's 2020 Gold Update and Yearbook Presentation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OWNX0_Q6H80)), the PGM Yearbook on 30 June 2020 ([CPM Group's 2020 Platinum Group Metals PGM Market Update and Yearbook…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dYlXqaZ6hds)), and the cycle closed with the 2021 Gold Annual Update preview on 12 March 2021 ([CPM 2021 Gold Annual Update – Preview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wUgha4xiu6M)). The fast clock is a commentary drumbeat that peaked in 2020 at nearly one video every two weeks: two "Gold Trade Signal and Recommendation" clips within four days (8 June and 12 June 2020) ([CPM Gold Trade Signal and Recommendation - Jeffrey Christian](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KzmKuzuz2DQ), [CPM Gold Trade Signal and Recommendation - Jeffrey Christian](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jbWsOJYnrtg)), another trade call on 14 July ([CPM Gold Trade Recommendation and why the metal will not reach $10,00…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qjkFnDZ2YME)), a "stand aside" call on 27 July ([CPM Gold Trade Recommendation: Why It Is Time To Stand Aside - Jeffre…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=efUpv9lqFe8)), and then an almost metronomic fortnightly rhythm through the autumn — 16 October, 30 October, 6 November, 20 November, 4 December, 11 December ([The Apples and Oranges of Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oQQytRMbzcg), [Backfield In Motion For Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2KmnouE61Yg), [How High Can Gold Go After the US Election?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nlSXt8Fkww0), [Profit and Protect Your Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1CANPjTFnH8), [Politics and Gold, The Lessons of 1933](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PVznAwB10mQ), [Gold's Place In An Overly Optimistic 2021](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I7AYzgLgTC8)).

The recycled material is easy to name: the myth-versus-reality framing. "Gold: Myth vs Reality" from 17 July 2020 ([CPM Group - Gold: Myth vs Reality - Jeffrey Christian](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DtuyP7NiPsg)) reappears wholesale in "Silver Fact and Fantasy" on 4 March 2021 ([CPM  Webinar: Silver Fact and Fantasy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrzpZKm-oGc)) and its companion piece on CPM's "Record On Silver, Process, Research, and Manipulation Theories" a day earlier ([CPM Group’s Record On Silver, Process, Research, and Manipulation The…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bxcPKsYf25o)); the 23 February 2021 rebuttal of a silver contract default ([CPM Group - Silver Futures Contract Default Not Likely - Jeffrey Chri…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C1EYmE719jY)) re-litigates ground CPM had already covered at the squeeze's height on 29 January ([CPM Group: Silver, Gamestop, and WallStreet Bets: What we know.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N54_h29SeUY)). The deep-read evidence confirms the pattern brutally: 12 June 2020, 29 October 2021, 9 August 2022, and 5 August 2025 are all flagged as recurring, and the 29 October 2021 item is scored as containing "nothing" new at all. Notably, the recycling is of framework, not stance — within six weeks in mid-2020 the posture swung from capping expectations (the 14 July video arguing gold would not reach the five-figure price in its title) to "All Roads Lead To Gold" on 21 August and "No One Should Be Short On Gold" on 31 August ([CPM Group - All Roads Lead To Gold - Jeffrey Christian](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vNkMV4Je9Fk), [CPM Group - No One Should Be Short On Gold - Jeffrey Christian](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fRzghWogdJg)), a flip the digest records but does not explain.

Genuinely new information enters almost exclusively through exogenous shocks or through the firm's own affairs rather than fresh market analysis. News-driven additions include the ETF-holdings piece on 11 September 2020 ([CPM Group - Changing Dynamics In ETF Holdings - Jeffrey Christian](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X7l3Jq4O5uw)), the post-election treatment on 6 November, the 1933 political parallel on 4 December, an unusual rhodium pitch on 20 January 2021 ([CPM - Who Should Be Investing In Rhodium?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sK-K96qJLh8)), and the January 2021 Reddit-silver moment. Per the deep-read, the only new content inside the flagged recurring items is a business update (increased consulting demand, 12 June 2020), an account of a meeting with Wall Street Silver (9 August 2022), and a rebuttal to a comment-section critic who claimed a silver promoter knows more than CPM Group (5 August 2025). The pattern is telling: novelty arrives on the consulting-revenue and feud side of the ledger, while the market argument itself keeps circling the same myth-busting core — an introduction video from 18 August 2020 suggests the shop was simultaneously recruiting a new audience for old material ([Introduction To CPM Group](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g7zSiFjuYuM)).

The explicit "something has changed" moments are rare and quotable, and both come from outside the market commentary proper. On 12 June 2020 the change was commercial: "we found ourselves providing increased volumes of consulting." On 9 August 2022 it was interpersonal: "I met with Jim Lewis of Wall Street Silver" — the author engaging directly with a critic rather than rebutting him in the abstract. The 5 August 2025 entry is flagged as new but carries no quoted change declaration in the evidence, so whether the author framed it as a turning point is unverifiable here. On cadence: within 2020 the reuse cycle is roughly fortnightly; around the yearbook months it is annual; and the recurring flag persists at roughly yearly intervals out to 2025 even as archive density collapses — the visible timeline runs only to 12 March 2021, the archive holds 54 items of which just 31 are dated here, and the post-2021 deep-read items come without links, so the late-period picture is thin and should be read as provisional.

study/cpm-group/topic/silver-supply-and-.text:
CPM Group's silver coverage is, by its own architecture, a rerun. The load-bearing claim — that refined supply comfortably covers fabrication demand, and that deficit and shortage talk is narrative rather than arithmetic — predates the video archive itself. A deep-read from August 2015 already has Jeffrey Christian citing the "advent of LED lighting for example" and "demand reduction due to the higher prices" as the real story, while conceding only that "people expect that the supply increases to continue." A decade on, in November 2025, the sentence is nearly unchanged: "Newly refined silver production from mine production and from secondary recovery from scrap continues to outstrip fabrication dem[and]." The delivery vehicle runs on an annual spring cadence — the [2019 Silver Yearbook Launch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-jGHFUKTio) in April 2019, the [Annual Silver Update](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bo8jT0XPcbM) in May 2021 (re-delivered wholesale for a different audience as the [2021 Silver Update for Chinese Markets](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hklab62wIy0) two months later), the [2024 Silver Market Outlook](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AutbJDWZfr0), and [Silver Facts And Fantasies 2025](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W5ReHm2dbLk) in March 2025. Even a July 2021 title shrugs at the loop: [Gold and Silver: It Is Still All About Demand](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o0Vb7ZwJfzs).

Title reuse is the clearest fingerprint of the recycling. "How Much Silver Is Really Available" ran on [September 15, 2023](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IPMS5mYzvXE) and again, verbatim, on [January 16, 2024](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xD7w6o21Ujk) — four months apart. [The Truth About Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCZKS5WVbsw) (May 2023) became [The Truth About Silver Demand and Price](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7ypNBIi2LAE) (February 2024). The "Facts and Fantasies" brand stamps three videos in twelve months: [March 5, 2024](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4XYHRtWy3GQ), [March 15, 2024](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jh0Mv34sa6w), and [March 18, 2025](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W5ReHm2dbLk). Around these flagships sits an event-driven rebuttal cycle that fires whenever prices spike or shortage chatter trends: [Silver, Gamestop, and WallStreet Bets](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N54_h29SeUY) in January 2021; the 2022 inventory double-tap of [The Relationship Between The Silver Price, Inventories, and Comex Positions](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HFQ9NuYCmDY) and [Low Silver Inventories Do Not Cause High Silver Prices](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=71QcOEr8EaE); [Silver Deficits Don't Exist And Other Silver Myths](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k7muhimpCms) in August 2023; [The Silver Shortage Chimera](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9SpxKkghmu4) in April 2024; and, in February 2025, [Silver Déjà Vu: Why Prices Spiked Higher And What Comes Next](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6V-f8U28HGM) — a title that openly concedes the rerun. Quiet stretches (mid-2021 through early 2022) coincide with quiet prices; 2023–2025 run at roughly one silver video a month.

Genuinely new material is scarce, and only one deep-read is flagged as non-recurring: the February 2022 comparison of Berkshire Hathaway's 1998 silver purchase to modern "drain the swamp" theories — an actual new argument. The rest of the novelty is empirical. May 2021 brought the LBMA clerical error, aired days after the yearbook launch: "london inventories are 116 million ounces less than somebody mistakenly said they were at the end of march," promptly defused with "the mistake as egregious as it was... is actually not important to the real silver market." April 2022 added a named-price rebuttal of a specific promoter. April 2023 added supply-response data ("Chinese production in 2022 seems to have been static," "only one small project started production in Indonesia"). March 2024 contributed coin-market color on Maple Leafs versus Eagles; April 2024 a margin comparison ("the profit margin on primary silver producers last year was about 29%"). March 2025 pulled in macro plumbing — "we have 40 million ounces of record gold uh inventories" (the transcript says gold mid-silver-talk, which tells you how interchangeable the inventory template is) and "we've seen some central banks starting to move gold into the New York Fed." November 2025 added a fresh estimate: "This year we're looking at about 135 million ounces of investment demand on a net basis."

The moments the author says something *has* changed are telling, because the changes are almost always on the other side of the debate. In 2015 the changes were structural — LED lighting, price-driven demand destruction. By June 2021 the change was merely terminological: "some people now call that a primary deficit." In April 2022 it was promoter behavior: "now he's touting thousand ounce bars," "charging like 31 or 32 or 33 dollars an ounce," while "our clients were buying silver thousand ounce bars... at 29 not at 31 or 32 or 33." In September 2025 it was price: "They got up to $45.90 some odd cents earlier this morning" — followed instantly by the insistence that nothing else had: "we're not particularly seeing tight supplies... the supply is really not that tight." By November 2025 a real change finally registered on the demand side — "The silver market for the smaller investment products has been gutted by sales" — though the supply conclusion stayed put. Four deep-reads are flagged flatly as new="nothing" (August 2015, April 2024, September 2025, and one of two November 2025 passes). The cadence, in short: an annual flagship, spike-triggered rebuttals, and perhaps two genuinely new facts a year — a framework with fixed supply meeting an argument environment that, from CPM's chair, never really changes either.

study/cpm-group/topic/macroeconomic-outl.text:
The macroeconomic-outlook file is less an argument than a franchise with a refresh schedule. The archive runs from a lone 2015 oil-market video ([What You Need To Know About The Oil Market](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6FepdXXoaNs)) through near-silence until December 2020 ([CPM Group - Gold's Place In An Overly Optimistic 2021](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I7AYzgLgTC8)), then settles into a roughly monthly cadence from 2022 onward, with bursts of twice-monthly output in late May/early June 2023 ([CPM Market Outlook](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=klUnij1aNw0), [Market Update: The Truth About the Economy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GG2yfKiZPzc)) and January 2025 ([Gold and Silver Price Insurance](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BUltNqTHmm0), [Disaster Recovery, Recessions, and Metals](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kd-9enetTGY)). The deep-read makes the recycling explicit: of fifteen closely-dated entries, fourteen are flagged recurring, one (June 30, 2023) is bluntly logged as containing "nothing" new, and the only non-recurring item in the whole set is the January 4, 2021 vaccination clock — "it's going to take at least six months for a significant enough portion of the population... to be vaccinated" — which is a pandemic timeline, not a macro thesis.

The recycled spine is recession timing, and it is a treadmill. By August 2021 the framing was already apocalyptic in title if not in substance ([The Imminent Economic Collapse](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sRqbuPl9c_k)). In May 2022 came the one genuinely new argument of that stretch — a 1987-crash analogy used to argue equity volatility didn't mean imminent recession — wrapped around the recurring call that "recession is obviously coming, but it could be two years away," which echoed through that summer's videos ([How Inflation, Interest Rates and Recession May Affect Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=10zL22_Y39s), [How Long The Recession Will Last](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zp8K-lh1Bu4)). By November 2022 the date had slipped — "it is most likely uh that it would be 2024 2025," with the author noting "we've seen various banks mark down their probabilities of a recession starting in 2023." October 2023 repeated the same 2024–2025 expectation ([Preparing For The Next Recession](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JuUnsDXzh9k)), now garnished with "Global growth slowing" and "industrial production has slowed." In December 2023 the herd itself became the story: consensus had swung from "we're about to fall into a recession" to "there's not going to be a recession," and "now we're starting to see Market consensus shift back to well there could be a recession in 2024." The forecast only hardened in 2025 — February's "the potential for a recession in the next 12 to 24 months... has increased" and pressures "indicative of potential recession sooner rather than later" grown "more prominent over the last nine months" ([What Really Happens To Gold During A Recession](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IkdJaAIn7II)), then May's sharpest self-revision in the corpus, "We have increased the depths of the recession that we are projecting" ([U.S. GDP Shrinks](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jJ-9wWwfojQ)), then September's stretch of duration: "we do see problems continuing and we see them continuing for a longer period of time than we had been have been projecting."

Genuinely new material almost always arrives as a data release dropped into the reused frame. January 6, 2023 was the December jobs report — "they showed a strong economy 223 new thousand new jobs created," with the wrinkle that "markets didn't necessarily take it that way they said oh this is kind of weak" ([Gold and Silver Prices Jump On Jobs Report](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YopGzQ_iFds)). May 31, 2023 was the data-dense outlier: M2's percent change going negative ("it's never been negative before but now it is"), month-to-month CPI back in its pre-2021 range, and unemployment "the lowest that it's been since like the 1960s." June 2023 added Fed stress tests — 23 systemically important banks absorbing a $540 billion loss — even as the same date is elsewhere logged as containing nothing new, a contradiction worth holding onto. October 2023 contributed record Treasury demand: "interest rates have risen bond prices have fallen," yet "demand for the US Treasury Securities bonds and notes and t- bills has not declined it's actually risen," feeding the long-running debt thread ([The Debt To Fear](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gPw0A4N34P8), [What The US Debt Means](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-PCuBTkczDs)). The dollar thread repeats the same way — "Dollars not crashing yet sorry for those who were impatient for it" in January 2023, versus a rising-dollar video a year earlier ([What The Rising Dollar Means For Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TBXzM5GSB_w)) — until September 2024 quantified it: up "1.7% last Friday from where it had been in January" and "2.9% from... September 20th of 2023." The mid- and late-2024 entries survive only in Chinese-language transcripts (a Reuters survey in June, with 18% of central-bank reserve managers planning to add dollar holdings; November's foreign Treasury holdings of $8.67 trillion, up $170 billion in September alone ([The Future of Gold and Silver Prices](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=21tRkw9MKkI))). March 2025 brought the one stagflationary print — "It showed uh weaker economic activity and higher inflation" — with gold at $3,124, and May 2025 added tariff front-loading: "demand was brought forward into the first quarter and into March by investors buying automobiles and other goods in advance of" anticipated tariffs.

The shape of the debate is a forecast that never resolves, only re-dates: from May 2022 through late 2023 the recession sits perpetually one-to-two years out, and the real inflection doesn't come until 2025, when the language flips from timing to severity and duration — at which point the "new" content is still mostly fresh numbers in an old argument. The author's posture is consistent throughout and mildly contrarian: skeptical of collapse-mongers (the May 2023 "Charlatans" title, the snark at dollar-crash "impatience") while maintaining a slow-rolling recession call. Two corpus caveats: the deep-read runs to September 2025 while the archive stops in mid-June 2025 ([Middle East Tensions](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kC0W0g9WhL0)), so recent months are thinly covered, and with fourteen of fifteen sampled entries flagged recurring, the reuse count likely understates rather than overstates the pattern.

study/cpm-group/topic/geopolitics-and-po.text:
Jeffrey Christian's geopolitics coverage runs on an event clock, not a calendar. The archive holds a single 2021 entry ([Worldwide Risks, Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MMzgPml9Kho), September 10) before Russia's invasion of Ukraine trips the series into a weekly rhythm: seven videos in five weeks from March 8 to April 12, 2022 — the initial rally call as [Russia Looks For Buyers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=20QsWnUrRD0), the [long-term commodity outlooks after Russia](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JutgSZHugvQ), two March war-market updates, then the April run on [Russian gold and the ruble](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7q88UbXPoC0) and ["Often Amazed, But Never Surprised"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7QRS6YAiqto). Across the entire deep-read record, exactly one video is flagged as genuinely new rather than recurring — the March 18, 2022 installment ([The Wartime Market: Why Gold and Silver Prices Are Not Reacting The W…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=77RCqH8YI64)), and even its title concedes the war-risk template wasn't working. That is where Christian declares a regime change three times over: "we are in a wartime market," that Putin "has destroyed russia's stature on the world plate stage," and that the war "demonstrated that there are numerous problems with their much vaulted uh military restructuring."

The Russian-gold thread is the most heavily recycled material in the file. It launches with the April 2022 ruble pieces, resurfaces through the [European natural gas scare](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrJeb7JfHxY) of October 2022 and the [Wagner-era unrest](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jOMCS0SJHW4) of June 2023, and by an August 9, 2024 deep-read (recurring, but with new documentation — the archive itself skips from July to October that year) Christian is reporting that "俄罗斯一直在用黄金为其政府、国家和战争提供资金" — Russia has been funding its state and the war with gold since 2022 — while its central bank avoids dollars and euros ("俄罗斯央行尽可能避免使用美元和欧元作为资金"). Two months later the theme gets its question-mark reprise in [Will Russian Gold Flood The Market - Should Investors Be Worried?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VR5YhXKP6XU). The other substantive update lands November 11, 2022, when he revises the war's trajectory: "Russia's marching toward losing the war," with "signs of internal dissent" inside Russia and a Chinese "hard line has become even harder" — a genuinely shifted assessment, though still flagged recurring because the frame (what does Russia mean for metals) never changed.

The domestic-politics thread repeats on a four-year election clock with filler between. ["How High Can Gold Go After the US Election?"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nlSXt8Fkww0) (November 6, 2020) recurs as ["Gold and Silver After 2024 Elections"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i5VkhPikqoo) (November 15, 2024), with [The Cost of Political Dysfunction](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7W3jEZqWWGQ), [Political Turmoil And What Comes Next](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HGZgA8ooH2Q) and [The Politics Of Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OSSy8tfVqEE) as intermediate installments. Between elections he reaches for historical analogy — [Politics and Gold, The Lessons of 1933](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PVznAwB10mQ) — which matches the deep-read finding that his 2015 oil-market material (predating this archive) was already recycling "the first big increase in oil prices came in 1973" and the arrival of "institutional hot money," in a video whose new-information field reads, flatly, "nothing." The same 2015 reads had OPEC having "lost some of its market power over the last 10 years" and "Saudi Arabia has said to OPEC we will keep our production hi" — material that resurfaces neatly in the June 2024 [Saudi Oil Impact](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6JvZ4Uhb6Es) update. Around the 2024 vote, a deep-read dated November 19 flags one change only: "我们消除了一个不确定因素——总统人选确定" — the single uncertainty of the presidency has been removed. The follow-through on January 10, 2025 bolts fresh numbers onto the deficits-drive-gold frame: employment data that "came in very good," Elon Musk's doubts about budget cuts, and "interest rates have been rising over the last week or so."

The Middle East and tariff thread shows the recycling at its most mechanical — and where it visibly strains. [How War Between Israel And Iran Could Impact Gold And Silver Prices](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H3KpZZ9_pnI) (October 2024) and [Will Tariffs Extend The Bull Market?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KYxf_7fcHgs) (April 2025) re-run the war-risk template; the June 13, 2025 surge video ([Gold And Silver Prices Surge: Economic Concerns As Middle East Tensio…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kC0W0g9WhL0)) carries the sharpest genuinely new claim in the late record — that the London meeting produced only an "agreement was that they would continue to talk," contradicting "the US government saying that the tariff trade war" had been resolved. By March 2026 the frame breaks in public: prices ["Jump As War Risk Grows"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U_W0iRucHyg) on March 10, then ["Are Falling Despite Iran Conflict Escalati…"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jl8g4HfCWzA) one week later — same conflict, opposite arrows, which is the clearest evidence that this is a format rather than a forecast. The spring 2026 cluster then rotates the standing cast of state actors — [India warning citizens off gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hk3kpcMhsEY), [China mattering "more than ever"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H8jB9O1y_nk), a [CIA-gold silver update](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2UJgqCeQ_fU) — before settling back into the evergreen warning mode of ["New Risks Are Building Fast!"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-RRUlGQb6o).

The net cadence: one geopolitical video in quiet years (2021) versus seven or eight in shock years (2022, 2024), compressing to weekly only during acute episodes like the March–April 2022 invasion cluster and the May–June 2026 run; mid-cycle years are bridged by war-plus-rates hybrids like [War, Interest Rates, and Alerts](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0jhdk5xt6JI), the [China-and-Japan commentary](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KD0RCTD9zDI) and ["Silver Plated Missiles"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rniBAo17ZhI). Of the eight deep-reads, only March 18, 2022 is wholly new; the rest are recurring frames with dated updates bolted on. One caveat worth stating plainly: the deep-read evidence samples eight videos against a 31-item archive, two of them from 2015 before the archive even begins, so the novelty judgments here rest on a thin slice of the series.

study/cpm-group/topic/monetary-policy-an.text:
Across 29 videos from January 2021 to June 2026, CPM Group's monetary-policy commentary is less a chain of arguments than a small stock of theses restated on a schedule. The rates-versus-gold explainer is the workhorse: it surfaces as [CPM Group - Interest Rates: Gold's Most Complicated and Important Rel…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y39eAhDCdI4) in January 2021, [Why Interest Rates Won't Hurt Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RiRYdTEmEpw) in August 2021, [How Interest Rates May Affect Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=im271XZWR18) in May 2022, [What Future Lower Interest Rates Mean For Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ju03xyxarVk) in December 2023, and [Gold And Silver Market Update: Why Interest Rate Changes May Mislead …](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-6Zt6_Rj4EQ) in June 2026 — roughly an annual rerun with only the sign of the rate move flipped. The gold-versus-inflation explainer runs on the same clock: [The Real Relationship Between Gold and Inflation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5o9BHtiXJ_M) (October 2021), [What Makes Gold An Excellent Hedge Against Inflation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kYkxdMHkAG0) (August 2022), [What Inflation Means For Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4nHl7qMQnKk) (September 2022), and [Gold And Inflation: It's Not So Simple](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aiGDIKClJT8) (February 2023). A third template — the inflation-recession-outlook combo — recurs in [How Inflation, Interest Rates and Recession May Affect Gold and Silve…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=10zL22_Y39s) (June 2022), [2024 Gold And Silver Forecast: Inflation, Recession, and Profiting Fr…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3BGoTQ7i_vg) (May 2024), and [Gold And Silver Market Update: Inflation, Recession, and Precious Met…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XmWL2vGkk-o) (April 2025). Even the punchline is recycled: [Why Lower Inflation Will Lead To Higher Gold and Silver Prices](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lzZ7Thf5OVE) (December 2022) and [Gold and Silver Soar As Inflation Falls Flat: This Is Why](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fo9SbQlJbdc) (November 2023) are the same disinflation-is-bullish argument twelve months apart.

The cadence tracks the inflation cycle, not the ideas. The titled archive is dormant after January 2021 until late August, then runs hot — eight videos in the final twenty weeks of 2021 and ten across 2022, close to biweekly — before thinning to five in 2023, two each in 2024 and 2025, and one in 2026.
