The deep reads confirm the recycling: of ten segments examined, only the May 14, 2021 treatment of the April CPI/PPI release is flagged as non-recurring, and it contains the archive's last genuinely new analytical points — the base-effect argument ("you're measuring it against april 2020 which was the beginning of the lockdown") and the observation that "the core inflation figures were actually higher than the headline figures which is unusual." After that, "new" means whatever print just landed. An August 13, 2021 segment is marked new = nothing, its only changes a record in Fed reverse-repo volumes and a Gary Gensler regulatory aside; September 24, 2021's novelty is one CPI report ("the only component of the cpi that was up more than two percent was petroleum-based energy"; used autos "actually was down about one and a half percent") plus the dot plot; March 18, 2022 and January 6, 2023 are both new = nothing outright. The lone lane-change is a late-2021 detour into [Nostalgia For A Gold Standard That Never Was](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gTCGEdqDwWk) and [What the Constitution REALLY says about Gold and Silver](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDU7yndPMC0), after which it is back to CPI-and-Fed material. The one new exogenous variable is war, which enters the frame in April 2022 ([Gold and Silver Prices Rise as Inflation and War Take Its Toll, This …](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jWAqgYvBuV0)); the closest things to new arguments are title-level tweaks — [The Rise Of Gold: More Than Just Inflation (Part 1)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jk5ZPSXui3Y) in February 2022 and the "Not So Simple" walk-back of the simple hedge framing in February 2023.

The "something has changed" moments cluster on data days, and the author flags each one. September 24, 2021: the Fed "basically agreed with that" transitory framing, projecting rates "up to about two percent by 2023" — a shift the channel then headlines as [Gold and Silver Are Adjusting To A New Monetary Policy Regime](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0obgfA3eB0Q). December 14, 2021, in [Gold and Silver Show Weakness As Concerns Over Inflation Rise, What W…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L_igFqCmfZI): "the producer price index data came out for the united states and it was very high," so "gold and silver fell and they fell significantly" and "silver broke below 22," with money-supply growth cited "around 65 percent." March 18, 2022: "the feds said hey we're going to be even more aggressive fighting inflation than everybody thought," with "six… interest rate hikes" expected. May 20, 2022 brings the first real turn — "inflation data has started to peak and turn down," and Ukraine "may develop in a way that further reduces the war premium." November 11, 2022: the market's "most probable expectation… is another 50 basis point increase" in December followed by 25s, on "signs of peaking inflation," feeding directly into December's lower-inflation-is-bullish thesis. January 6, 2023: the Fed "doesn't see the inflation going away anytime soon" and would be "lucky if they get down to about five percent."

The loudest change-flags come at the end of the covered evidence. On December 1, 2023 the author declares the regime over: "The FED has stopped raising interest rates," "interest rates do look like they're Peak they peaked," and "what's happened interest rates have fallen" — "now they're down to about 4.2%" on the ten-year, with long rates having "come down much more sharply" than short rates and cuts expected "sometime in the march to May period of time." That is the last deep-read in the digest; what follows — [Precious Metals Update: How Inflation and Fed Policies Affect Gold an…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZHxPejxwviU) (August 2024), the April 2025 outlook, and [Gold, Silver, and the Fed's Warning of What's Coming Next](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hgp1yn1I-Y8) (October 2025) — looks from titles alone like the old templates relabeled, but there is no transcript evidence after December 2023, so whether anything new entered post-pause cannot be established here. What the record does show is a fixed framework (rates don't mechanically hurt metals; the inflation link is complicated) re-run against each fresh print, while the framing itself whipsaws: [Critical Time For Silver as Inflation Wanes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AbmjEzDxiGY) in November 2021 gives way within weeks to rising-inflation worry and then [Prepare For Higher Interest Rates and Lower Gold and Silver prices - …](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3iijoftbjEk) in January 2022 — a tension with August 2021's rates-won't-hurt thesis the archive never explicitly resolves.

study/cpm-group/topic/central-bank-gold-.text:
Central bank gold is a workhorse topic in this archive — thirteen pieces between April 2021 and February 2026, arriving in bursts rather than on a steady drumbeat. Three landed in 2021 alone: the Hungarian purchase story in April ([The Impact of Hungarian Central Bank purchases and record London inve…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tn8tkU67WHE)), a practices overview in June ([Central Bank Gold Practices; US Debt and Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fimg7ZB8wGA)), and a "central banks seen waiting to buy" piece in October ([Central Banks Seen Waiting To Buy More Gold](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFUYu5z2xm8)). The topic then thinned out — the Russia question of June 2022 ([Has Russia Just Sold Its Gold?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4LQa4a0hNgM)), a China-reserves dig in January 2023 ([Uncovering the Truth Behind China's Gold Reserves & Silver Mine Reser…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BNUrHI4gHNY)), and a back-to-basics explainer in September 2023 ([Central Bank Gold Buying Explained](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NLGWwaA8hYU)) — before 2024 became the densest year, with five pieces from January through November. The recycled spine never moves: who is buying, who is holding back, and why central banks want the metal at all, restated most nakedly in August 2024's "Why Central Banks Own Gold And Investors Should Too" ([link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ETnOdXK0jLM)).

The deep-read flags confirm the recycling pattern: nearly every dated entry is marked recurring, and the "new" material inside them is mostly data refreshes and rebuttals rather than new frameworks. On 2023-02-22 the contribution was rebutting claims about central banks "dumping" the dollar, with the author complaining "there's a tremendous amount of misinformation about Central Bank activity both with the dollar and with gold." By January 2024 ([Gold Market Update: Central Bank Buyers and Sellers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=soQnqRYSKeU)) he was correcting his own numbers — "2022 did not see 20 million ounces that was a mistake... our view was it was about 10.2 million ounces" — while tallying the fresh 2023 data ("China has reported December and they bought another 290,000... so they their purchases uh are about 7.2 7.3 million ounces"), naming the sellers (Turkey, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan), and clarifying that no central bank is plotting a return to the gold standard. March 2024's addition was similarly evergreen: silver stays out of reserves because its market is too small.

Genuinely new arguments are scarcer. The only deep-read entry flagged non-recurring is 2024-08-09 ([Which Central Banks Are Not Buying Gold And Why It Matters To You](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UGckn7Inkww)): Ghana enters the story — "加纳... 找到柴油进口商，表示如果进口商愿意，可以用黄金而不是美元支付柴油货款" (Ghana approached diesel importers offering payment in gold rather than dollars) — a stress case of gold as payment for essentials, paired with the blunt pushback "不，实际上，大多数中央银行的黄金储备都非常低" against tales of heavy African accumulation. The same episode flagged a behavioral turn — "过去一年，尤其是自四月以来几个月的高金价，改变了央行的黄金买卖活动" — plus a cautionary tale about a bank that decided to buy in 2010 and "至今仍未开始购买黄金," which undercuts survey-based predictions. The other real pivot is 2025-03-28: "That's a 40% decline in the volume of gold being purchased," with the baton passing outright — "It's been investment demand, strong investment demand that has driven the gold price" — a reweighting that September 2024's both-drivers framing ([Central Bank and Investor Demand Are Driving Gold Prices Higher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DJbciTJrSms)) hadn't anticipated.

The explicit "this has changed" moments, in order: the narrative turning misinformation-heavy (Feb 2023); China's 7.3-million-ounce total, the 2022 correction, and the transparency claim — "there's been a great increase in uh transparency on the part of central banks over the last 20 or 30 years" — plus "China... made an announcement of changing their attitudes toward gold" (Jan 2024); price-driven behavior change (Aug 2024); and the 40% decline with investment demand taking over (Mar 2025). Note the transparency argument itself gets recycled: announced in January 2024, it resurfaces as the thesis of February 2026's [Central Bank Gold: Secrecy To Transparency](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZeV-xWUOjy8), with the secrecy angle already teased in November 2025's [A Secret Plan To Buy Gold? What Central Banks Are Really Doing](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K4B0f0LUn-0) — the same point arriving in new clothes two years later. One caveat: the 2021–22 items, the late-2024 cluster ([The Countries Still Boosting Gold Reserves, And What They Have In Com…](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FpyNS_gfSX4)), and the 2025–26 pieces are titles only in this digest, so fine-grained reuse inside them can't be verified here.
